{
  "summary": "This pull request adds an opt-in `=bip152-hb` suffix to the `-addnode` startup option, allowing operators to manually specify outbound peers that should immediately and permanently be requested to send BIP152 high-bandwidth compact block announcements. Connections matching these configured endpoints are sent `SENDCMPCT(high_bandwidth=true)` on handshake and upon reconnect, operating outside of and in addition to the automatic three-peer compact block rotation. The option is validated at startup to ensure it is not used in conjunction with `-blocksonly`.",
  "problem": "Node operators cannot manually designate specific peers for high-bandwidth compact block relay based on out-of-band network topology knowledge. Currently, Bitcoin Core only selects up to three high-bandwidth peers dynamically based on who delivers blocks first, meaning low-latency peering links or private multi-site nodes must wait for automatic selection and risk losing their status upon reconnection.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'an operator may run nodes in multiple locations or maintain a stable, low-latency peering link and want that connection to announce compact blocks immediately and consistently, including after reconnects, instead of waiting for automatic selection.'"
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],

  },
  "scope_notes": "Refactors how -addnode options are passed into CConnman via AddedNodeParams structs, moving the v2 transport decision from CConnman::Init() to init.cpp.",
  "changed_since_previous": "",
  "card": "This pull request allows node operators to designate specific outbound added nodes as BIP152 high-bandwidth compact block peers via a new =bip152-hb suffix on -addnode. Currently, Bitcoin Core automatically selects up to three high-bandwidth peers dynamically, preventing operators with dedicated low-latency peering links or multi-region nodes from guaranteeing immediate compact block announcements. Configured peers receive high-bandwidth requests at handshake and across reconnects without displacing or entering the dynamic three-peer rotation pool. Evidence of importance is limited to the author's description of operational needs for multi-datacenter node setups and dedicated peerings.",

result.summary: This pull request adds an opt-in `=bip152-hb` suffix to the `-addnode` startup option, allowing operators to manually specify outbound peers that should immediately and permanently be requested to send BIP152 high-bandwidth compact block announcements. Connections matching these configured endpoints are sent `SENDCMPCT(high_bandwidth=true)` on handshake and upon reconnect, operating outside of and in addition to the automatic three-peer compact block rotation. The option is validated at startup to ensure it is not used in conjunction with `-blocksonly`.
result.problem: Node operators cannot manually designate specific peers for high-bandwidth compact block relay based on out-of-band network topology knowledge. Currently, Bitcoin Core only selects up to three high-bandwidth peers dynamically based on who delivers blocks first, meaning low-latency peering links or private multi-site nodes must wait for automatic selection and risk losing their status upon reconnection.
evidence: PR description: 'an operator may run nodes in multiple locations or maintain a stable, low-latency peering link and want that connection to announce compact blocks immediately and consistently, including after reconnects, instead of waiting for automatic selection.'
result.scope_notes: Refactors how -addnode options are passed into CConnman via AddedNodeParams structs, moving the v2 transport decision from CConnman::Init() to init.cpp.
result.card: This pull request allows node operators to designate specific outbound added nodes as BIP152 high-bandwidth compact block peers via a new =bip152-hb suffix on -addnode. Currently, Bitcoin Core automatically selects up to three high-bandwidth peers dynamically, preventing operators with dedicated low-latency peering links or multi-region nodes from guaranteeing immediate compact block announcements. Configured peers receive high-bandwidth requests at handshake and across reconnects without displacing or entering the dynamic three-peer rotation pool. Evidence of importance is limited to the author's description of operational needs for multi-datacenter node setups and dedicated peerings.
